There was an anti-Merkel protest in Berlin on 30 July - yes, almost 2 months ago, sorry for the huge delay - and I wanted to give you some insights into the German media on that occasion.

Some information about that afternoon. There was the anti-Merkel demonstration, there were around 3 counterdemonstrations, and there was also another event, a techno event called something like "procession of love".

I will start with something like an official source: RBB, that is the Berlin and Brandenburg branch of the ARD, the older and bigger of two public-service broadcasting networks in Germany. On their website I found two articles, here is one: Link

The headline says:

Demonstrations against 'Aufmarsch' of the right-wing populists

'Aufmarsch' is from the German original. Google translate offers

"deployment, marching up, march-past"

Some paper dictionary which I have offers

"marching up; line up; initial assembly; (strategic) concentration; deployment; parade, march-past"

I found cases where 'Aufmarsch' is used in a neutral, positive, or ironical sense, e.g. I found something about an "'Aufmarsch' of football legends", where it probably meant something like "parade of football legends", but normally it is used to carry a negative meaning. So the demonstrations of the Erdogan supporters in Cologne the next day were also generally called 'Aufmarsch'.

Or there is something else you can do: Search for 'Aufmarsch' in Google and then select 'Pictures'.

I will not translate it but will just use 'Aufmarsch' in the following.

This is what we read in the article about the anti-Merkel protesters:

  • 5x right-wing populists,
  • 2x nazis,
  • 4x neonazis,
  • 2x hooligans,
  • 2x intolerant,
  • 1x 'Aufmarsch',
  • 1x 'Hetze' (instigation, agitation, baiting; the German word carries a very negative meaning),
  • 1x racist,
  • sit-in blockades (suggested, might be a lie, see explanation below).

Now this is what we read about the counterprotesters:

  • Solidary,
  • open-minded ('offen' in the original),
  • cosmopolitan ('weltoffen'),
  • 2x tolerant,
  • democratic,
  • conservative ('bürgerlich', might be a lie, see explanation below).

Sit-in blockades

There is a strange phenomenon about sit-in blockades. In many articles about this afternoon one reads that there were sit-in blockades ("Sitzblockaden"), but no article says who held the sit-in blockades. Even searching the internet I was not able to find it out. But several articles, like the one from RBB mentioned above, mention the sit-in blockades in a paragraph which talks only about the anti-Merkel protesters. This suggests that the anti-Merkel protesters held the sit-in blockades. I wonder if that is true. If it is not true, then this style of reporting can be considered a lie.

Alliance of left-wing and conservative groups

Many articles say that the counterprotests were held by an alliance of left-wing and conservative groups. In the German originals they say 'bürgerlich', I think 'conservative' is the best possible translation. But is that true? I did not find any evidence that the counterprotests were held or supported by conservative groups. I only found evidence that the counterprotests were held by some notorious left-wing groups. It seems the media just made this "alliance of left-wing and conservative groups" up, so it looks as if the counterprotests were supported by basically everybody.
